# **How to Create a GitHub Repo and Push Code** 

# 

# **What is GitHub and why does it matter?**

**GitHub** is a platform where you can store your code online and manage your projects. It helps you keep track of changes, back up your work, and collaborate with other developers. GitHub is widely used in software development, making it easier to share code, contribute to projects, and showcase your work to employers or clients. It matters because it keeps your code organized, secure, and accessible from anywhere. 

## **Prerequisites**

Before you start, make sure you have:

* **A GitHub account** – This is where your code will be stored online.  
* **Git is installed on your computer**. Git is a tool that helps you save and track changes in your project.  
* **A code editor** – A program for writing and editing code, such as Visual Studio Code.  
* **A project folder** – Any folder on your computer that contains the files you want to upload to GitHub.  
* **An internet connection** – Needed to connect your computer to GitHub and upload your code.

Once these are ready, you can create your first GitHub repository and upload your project.

## **Create a GitHub Account**

If you do not already have a GitHub account, follow these steps:

### **Step 1: Open the GitHub Website**

Go to [GitHub](https://github.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com) in your web browser.

**What you should see:**  
 The GitHub homepage with a **Sign up** button.

![][image1]

### **Step 2: Click "Sign up"**

Click the **Sign up** button in the top-right corner of the page.

**What you should see:**  
 A registration form asking for your email address.

### **Step 3: Enter Your Email Address**

Type your email address and click **Continue**.

**What you should see:**  
 A field to create a password.

![][image2]

### **Step 4: Create a Password**

Choose a strong password that you can remember.

**Tip:** Use a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols for better security.

![][image3]

### **Step 5: Choose a Username**

Enter a unique username. This name will identify you on GitHub.

**Example:** ExampleUsername7867

**Tip:** If your username is already taken, GitHub will ask you to choose a different one. 

**![][image4]**

### **Step 7: Verify Your Account**

Complete the verification challenge shown by GitHub to confirm that you are a real person.

![][image5]

### **Step 7: Create Your Account**

Follow the remaining prompts and click **Create account**.

GitHub may send a verification code to your email address.

![][image6]

### **Step 8: Verify Your Email Address**

Open your email inbox, find the message from GitHub, and click the verification link or enter the verification code.

**What you should see:**  
 Your GitHub dashboard after verification is complete.![][image7]

### **Success\!**

### You now have a GitHub account and are ready to create your first repository and upload your code.

---

## **Install Git on Your Local Machine**

Before you can upload code to GitHub, you need to install **Git** on your computer.

**What is Git?**  
 Git is a tool that helps you track changes in your files and connect your computer to GitHub.

# **For Windows**

### **Step 1: Download Git**

Visit the official Git website:

[Git Downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Git should automatically detect that you are using Windows and offer the correct download.![][image8]

### **Step 2: Run the Installer**

Open the downloaded file and start the installation.

![][image9]

### **Step 4: Finish the Installation**

Click **Finish** when the installation is complete.

### **Step 5: Check That Git Is Installed**

Open **Command Prompt**:

1. Press **Windows \+ R**  
2. Type cmd  
3. Press **Enter**

Type:

git \--version

Press **Enter**.

**What you should see:**

git version 2.x.x

![][image10]

# **For macOS**

### **Step 1: Open Terminal**

Press **Command \+ Space** and search for **Terminal**.

### **Step 2: Check if Git Is Already Installed**

Type:

git \--version

Press **Enter**.

If Git is already installed, you will see a version number.

### **Step 3: Install Git (If Needed)**

If Git is not installed, macOS will usually show a message asking you to install the required developer tools.

Click **Install** and follow the instructions.

### **Step 4: Verify the Installation**

After installation finishes, run:

git \--version

You should now see the Git version number.

# **For Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)**

### **Step 1: Open Terminal**

Open the Terminal application from your system menu.

### **Step 2: Update Package Information**

Run:

sudo apt update

Press **Enter**.

### **Step 3: Install Git**

Run:

sudo apt install git

When asked to confirm,

 type: Y

and press **Enter**.

### **Step 4: Verify the Installation**

Run:

git \--version

**What you should see:**

git version 2.x.x

## **Common Issues**

**Tip:** If you see "`git` is not recognized as a command" on Windows, restart your computer and try again.

**Tip:** Make sure you type `git --version` exactly as shown, including the two dashes (`--`).

**Tip:** If the installation fails, download Git again from the official website and rerun the installer.

---

## **Configure Git (Set Your Name and Email)**

Before using Git, you need to tell it who you are. This helps Git mark your code changes with your name and email.

| Step | What You Do | Command Example | Why It Matters |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Set your name | git config \--global user.name "Your Name" | Shows who made the changes |
| 2 | Set your email | git config \--global user.email "you@example.com" | Links commits to your GitHub account |
| 3 | Check settings | git config \--global \--list | Confirms your details are saved |

## **Step 1: Open Terminal / Command Prompt**

* **Windows:** Open Command Prompt or Git Bash  
* **Mac:** Open Terminal  
* **Linux:** Open Terminal![][image11]

## **Step 2: Set Your Username**

Type this command:

git config \--global user.name "Your Name"

Replace **Your Name** with your real name.![][image12]

**Tip:** Use the same name you want to show on GitHub.

## **Step 3: Set Your Email**

Now type:

git config \--global user.email "youremail@example.com"

Replace it with the email you used to create your GitHub account.![][image13]

**Tip:** Make sure this email matches your GitHub account, or your commits may not link properly.

## **Step 4: Check Your Settings**

To confirm everything is set, run:

git config \--global \--list

You should see your name and email in the list.

## **Common Problems**

**Nothing shows after the command?**  
 That is normal. Git does not show a success message.

**Wrong name or email?**  
 Just run the same command again with the correct details.

---

# **Create a New Repository on GitHub**

A GitHub repository is an online folder where you can store and manage your project files. In this step, you will create your first repository to start saving and organizing your work on GitHub.

## **1\. Open GitHub**

Open your web browser and go to **github.com**.

If you are not already signed in, log in to your GitHub account.

**You should now see your GitHub homepage.![][image14]**

## **2\. Click the "+" Button**

Look at the **top-right corner** of the GitHub page.

You will see a **"+" (plus)** icon.

Click on it.

A small menu will appear.

From the menu, click **"New repository"**.

**You should now see the "Create a new repository" page.![][image15]**

**Tip:**

 If you cannot find the "+" button, make sure you are signed in to GitHub.

## **3\. Enter Your Repository Details**

You will now fill in some information about your repository.

### **Repository Name**

A **repository name** is the name of your project folder.

Type a simple name.

Example:

my-first-project

Try to keep the name short and easy to remember.

### **Description (Optional)**

A **description** is a short sentence that explains your project.

This step is optional, which means you can skip it if you want.

Example:

This is my first GitHub project.![][image16]**Tip:**  
Do not use very confusing or random names.  
A clear name makes your project easier to find later.

## **4\. Choose Public or Private**

You will now choose who can see your repository.

GitHub gives you two choices:

### **Public**

Anyone on the internet can view the repository.

### **Private**

Only you and the people you allow can view it.

If you are learning GitHub or building a portfolio, **Public** is usually a good choice.![][image17]

**Tip:**  
Many beginners accidentally choose **Private** and later wonder why others cannot see their project.

## **5\. Add a README File**

You will see an option called:

**"Add a README file"**

A **README** is a file that explains what your project is about.

It is usually the first thing people read when they visit your repository.

For beginners, you should **check this box**.

This makes GitHub create a starting file for you automatically.![][image18]

**Tip:**  
If you leave this unchecked, your repository will still work.  
But checking it makes the setup easier for beginners.

## **6\. Click "Create Repository"**

Check your information one more time.

Then click the **"Create repository"** button at the bottom of the page.

GitHub will create your repository.![][image19] 

# **Clone Repository Using HTTPS URL** 

In this step, you will download a copy of your GitHub repository onto your computer. This is called **cloning**, and it allows you to work on your project locally using Git and the terminal.

A **terminal** is a text-based tool used to run commands on your computer.

## **1\. Open Your GitHub Repository**

Go to GitHub and open the repository you created in the previous step.

You should now see your repository page.![][image20]

## **2\. Click the "Code" Button**

Look for the **"Code"** button near the top of the repository page.

Click on it.

A small menu will appear.![][image21]

## **3\. Select HTTPS**

Inside the menu, you will see different options for copying the repository link.

Click on **HTTPS** if it is not already selected.

**HTTPS** is a secure web link used to connect to GitHub.

You will now see a repository URL.

It will look similar to this:

https://github.com/your-username/my-first-project.git

Click the **copy** icon next to the URL.![][image22]

**Tip:**  
GitHub offers multiple connection methods like HTTPS and SSH.  
Beginners should use **HTTPS** because it is simpler to set up.

## **4\. Open the Terminal**

Now you need to open the **terminal** on your computer.

A terminal lets you type commands instead of clicking buttons.

### **Windows**

Open **Command Prompt**, **PowerShell**, or **Windows Terminal**.

### **Mac**

Open the **Terminal** app.

### **Linux**

Open the **Terminal** application.

![][image11]**Tip:**  
Do not worry if the terminal looks unfamiliar.  
You only need to type a few simple commands.

## **5\. Move to the Folder Where You Want the Project**

Before cloning, choose where you want the project folder to be stored.

Use the `cd` command.

`cd` means **change directory**, which means moving into a folder.

Example:https://github.com/username/my-first-project.git

cd Desktop

This command moves you to the Desktop folder.

![][image23]

**Tip:**  
If you skip this step, Git may clone the repository into a location you did not expect.

## **6\. Clone the Repository**

Now type the following command:

git clone repository-url

Replace `repository-url` with the GitHub link you copied earlier.

Example:

git clone https://github.com/your-username/my-first-project.git

Press **Enter**.

Git will start downloading the repository to your computer.

You should see messages showing the cloning process.

**Screenshot:** Running the git clone command in the terminal

**Tip:**  
If you see an error saying **"git is not recognized"**, Git may not be installed on your computer yet.

---

## **7\. Verify the Repository Was Cloned**

After cloning finishes, a new folder with your repository name will appear.

You can check this by typing:

ls

On Windows Command Prompt, you can also use:

dir

These commands show the files and folders in your current location.

You should see your repository folder in the list.
